slides.title: A Deployable Architecture for Robot-Mediated Tasks (DART): Evaluation in Socially Assistive Robot-Guided Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Exercises
slides.highlight: DART provides a cloud-based architecture to extend the capabilities of low-cost socially assistive robots for health interventions, supporting the RwB focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DART extends low-cost socially assistive robots using a web application and cloud infrastructure for complex tasks.
card.key_idea: A robot-agnostic architecture distributing interaction orchestration to a web app and data/computation to the cloud, while the robot handles physical embodiment and local motor control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via participatory design, an in-lab study (N=103), and a six-week in-home deployment (N=4) using SUS scores and psychological state metrics.
card.limitation: Participants identified speech input, visual presentation, and web–robot synchronization as priority areas for improvement.

slides.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a diagnostic benchmark for full-duplex dialogue that distinguishes between interruptions and backchannels, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ECHO is a diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex dialogue to evaluate context-sensitive turn-taking decisions.
card.key_idea: It uses matched-contrast pairs where the same user insertion is paired with different dialogue contexts to force a choice between Yielding and Keeping the floor.
card.evaluation: Evaluated four speech systems and Gemini (text reference) using Pairwise Action Success Rate (PASR); results show a strong Yield bias in most systems.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized audio rather than natural speech, and does not fully isolate dialogue context from acoustic factors like speaker-reference variation.

slides.title: Audio-Visual Turn-taking Prediction in Cocktail Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This research evaluates audio-visual turn-taking prediction models in cocktail-party scenarios, providing insights into modality-specific degradation and adaptation in noisy human interactions relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Audio-visual turn-taking models struggle with cocktail-party noise, but multimodal fine-tuning improves robustness.
card.key_idea: Evaluates Voice Activity Projection (VAP) variants (Audio, Video, Multimodal) by pre-training on clean Candor data and fine-tuning on noisy AVCocktail data to analyze domain adaptation.
card.evaluation: Tested on Candor and AVCocktail datasets using weighted F1 scores. Results show a 38% relative drop for clean-trained models in noise.
card.limitation: Fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of the original domain; high-level OpenFace features and current fusion methods limit peak performance.

slides.title: Exploring Multimodal Turn-Taking Cues in Face-to-Face Conversation using Voice Activity Projection
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that integrating visual features like facial action units, gaze, and pose improves turn-taking prediction over audio-only models, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Visual cues from face-to-face conversations significantly improve turn-taking prediction over audio-only models.
card.key_idea: Extends the Voice Activity Projection (VAP) transformer by fusing audio with visual features (FAU, gaze, head, body) using cross-attention, delta features, and trainable gating mechanisms.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 400 hours of Meta Seamless Interaction dataset using VAP loss and balanced accuracy for hold/shift, short/long, and pre-shift tasks.
card.limitation: Results may be upper-bound as test splits are not dyad-disjoint; gaze estimates are unreliable during eye occlusion.

slides.title: Learning to Refer from Estimated Listener Gaze
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING REFERRING EXPRESSIONS VIA ESTIMATED GAZE SCANPATHS
slides.highlight: This work uses estimated listener gaze scanpaths as learning signals to generate pragmatically optimal referring expressions, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: Finetuning VLMs using estimated listener gaze scanpaths generates more concise, pragmatically optimal referring expressions.
card.key_idea: A VLM speaker is optimized via RL using rewards derived from a neural listener (Molmo-REC-Gaze) that predicts human gaze fixations during comprehension.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via human listeners and Qwen2.5-VL across RefCOCO and RefOI datasets; gaze-based models reduced length from 15.4 to 4.0 words while increasing success to 80%.
card.limitation: A tradeoff exists between accuracy and verbosity; non-gaze listeners achieve higher success (86%) but produce significantly longer, less efficient references.

slides.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ROBOT PREFERENCE LEARNING VIA DYNAMIC IMPLICATION MODELING
slides.highlight: The proposed IMPLIED method improves how robots infer human preferences from feedback during collaboration, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: IMPLIED improves robot preference learning by dynamically revising implication labels for unchosen actions using feedback.
card.key_idea: A mixture model combining a fixed-rule prior with a Gaussian Process classifier that learns to infer and revise accepted/rejected labels for unchosen actions over time.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (sandwich-making, block-sorting) and a physical pizza-making study against fixed-rules and LLMs using L2 error, conflict proportion, and F1 scores.

slides.title: Self-Emergence Agent Architecture: Behavior-Inertia HMM, Reflexive Metacognition, and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling
slides.tldr: SELF-EMERGENCE AGENT ARCHITECTURE FOR STABLE PERSONALITY AND SOCIAL STRUCTURE
slides.highlight: This work introduces an architecture using a Hidden Markov Model and a metacognition loop to enable agents to develop stable personalities and social structures, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and adaptive AI teammates.

card.one_liner: SEAA enables LLM agents to develop stable, distinct personalities through a reflection-driven behavioral inertia loop.
card.key_idea: Integrates a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for behavioral inertia, where verbal metacognition updates HMM transition parameters, and social contrast drives self-other boundary formation.
card.evaluation: Tested via a numerical prototype (30 seeds) and DeepSeek-Chat; measured matrix divergence, personality determinism, and self-model distance against text-only controls.
card.limitation: The language-to-parameter mapping for HMM updates is identified as the main technical risk.

slides.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
slides.highlight: This work introduces MP-Bench to evaluate voice agents' turn-taking awareness and response appropriateness in multi-party contexts, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and group dynamics.

card.one_liner: MP-Bench evaluates voice agents' ability to participate in multiparty conversations via turn-taking and comprehension tasks.
card.key_idea: A benchmark using synthetic audio across Discussion and Turn-based Game scenarios to test turn-taking awareness (explicit, implicit, negative) and contextual response appropriateness.
card.evaluation: 12 voice agents were tested; results showed realtime models perform near chance on implicit turn-taking. LLM-judge results strongly correlate with human evaluation.
card.limitation: Uses synthetic audio without overlapping speech, background noise, or multi-turn engagement, creating a domain gap from real-world conversations.

slides.title: Negation Beyond the Verbal Channel: Temporal Multimodal Correlates in Dialogue
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that nonverbal behaviors, particularly facial features, can predict negation cues in dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Nonverbal behavior can distinguish spoken negation cues from control words without using lexical or acoustic data.
card.key_idea: Used time-series classifiers (e.g., RocketPFN) as probes on VR-captured multimodal streams (gaze, face, body) to analyze temporal and modality-specific correlates of negation cues.
card.evaluation: 10-fold cross-validation on 27 VR interviews. Strongest probes reached .75 mean AUROC; facial features were the most predictive modality.
card.limitation: Data is limited to a single VR survey setting and dominated by the German word 'nicht' (~80%).

slides.title: DiaWhisper-DPO: Role-Attributed Transcription of Clinical Interviews via Failure-Mined Preference Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces DiaWhisper-DPO, an end-to-end model for transcription and role attribution that reduces errors compared to cascaded diarization systems. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization within hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: DiaWhisper-DPO enables end-to-end role-attributed transcription of clinical interviews using failure-mined preference optimization.
card.key_idea: LoRA-tuned Whisper-large-v3 with an auxiliary role head, refined via DPO using genuine decoding failures as rejected completions and ground truth as chosen completions.
card.evaluation: Tested on DAIC-WOZ and PDCH-HAMD against cascaded baselines; achieved 0.973 role accuracy and 0.119 DER on DAIC-WOZ, showing high seed stability.
card.limitation: DAIC-WOZ evaluation relies on synthetic interviewer audio; outputs still require human verification for clinical use.

slides.title: Metacognitive Steering: Learning the Structure of Scientific Judgment
slides.tldr: INFERENCE-TIME CONTROLLER FOR SCIENTIFIC REASONING STRATEGIES
slides.highlight: This work introduces Metacognitive Steering to dynamically control a model's cognitive regime for exploration and critical reassessment, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition for adaptive agents.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive Steering enables dynamic control over a model's reasoning strategy using scientist interaction traces.
card.key_idea: An inference-time controller identifies cognitive regimes (exploration, convergence, scrutiny) from residual streams and applies layer-specific contrastive interventions to a frozen trillion-parameter MoE model.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via behavioral trajectory analysis and real-world tasks: identifying 8 BlueZ vulnerabilities and designing a propulsively landing solid-motor rocket.
card.limitation: Directly optimizing a sparse state detector could invite representation gaming and destabilize the underlying model.

slides.title: EMoG: Emotion-Modulated Gait Generation for Expressive Humanoid Locomotion
slides.highlight: EMoG enables humanoid robots to generate expressive, emotion-modulated walking patterns via an LLM-based parser, supporting more natural human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: EMoG enables humanoid robots to walk with continuously adjustable emotional styles while maintaining precise physical control.
card.key_idea: A lightweight MLP generates periodic gait trajectories conditioned on an emotional-style code and physical commands, tracked by a reinforcement learning policy and interfaced via an LLM parser.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via user recognition studies, MuJoCo simulations, and Unitree G1 hardware; demonstrated high completion rates and perceptible emotional cues across six styles.
card.limitation: Recognition accuracy varies by emotion category and decreases after physical execution; intensity is not yet perceptually calibrated.

slides.title: Mental Models in Human-AI Interaction: Methods and Challenges in the Generative and Agentic AI Era
slides.highlight: This workshop examines how users reason about and interact with AI systems, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on modeling human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A workshop proposal to reassess mental model research in the era of generative and agentic AI.
card.key_idea: The workshop aims to standardize mental model elicitation, clarify conceptual boundaries, and address challenges posed by the opacity and adaptivity of agentic AI systems.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text describes a proposed workshop program featuring lightning talks, peer elicitation exercises, and breakout discussions.
card.limitation: The construct is currently operationalized intuitively, using heterogeneous methods and overlapping concepts, which hinders research commensurability.

slides.title: Beyond "ChatGPT Can Make Mistakes": Designing Interventions to Support Metacognitive Monitoring in AI-Assisted Work
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE MONITORING INTERVENTIONS FOR AI ASSISTANCE
slides.highlight: This research explores interventions to support metacognitive monitoring in AI-assisted work, providing evidence on how specific design choices can reduce overconfidence and estimation error, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-monitoring.

card.one_liner: The paper proposes a design space for metacognitive interventions to improve human-AI confidence calibration.
card.key_idea: A design space organizing interventions by time (when), level (whose competence is judged), and source (who supplies the monitoring cue).
card.evaluation: Between-subjects experiment (N=917) using 12 planning problems. Reliability cards and contrasting replies reduced overconfidence, but no task-performance gains were found.
card.limitation: Interventions lowered usability, increased workload, and did not reliably improve task accuracy or within-item discrimination.

slides.authors: Manuel A. D. Santos et al.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior
slides.highlight: This work introduces a neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals across four ontological levels, supporting MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals across four ontological levels using hierarchical planning.
card.key_idea: A Hierarchical Planning Decoder attached to a frozen encoder, using soft neuro-symbolic regularization and hard reachability masks to ensure ontological validity.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15,002 multimodal episodes (NTU RGB+D 120); outperformed sequential baselines in top-5 accuracy and logical constraint satisfaction.
card.limitation: Challenges remain in compositional goal generalization and unordered set prediction.

slides.title: Travelxp Launches Marco Agentic AI Travel Concierge
slides.highlight: The launch of Marco, an agentic AI capable of bookings and payments, relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on agentic capabilities for human-AI teaming.

slides.title: Travelxp Launches Agentic AI Trip Concierge
slides.highlight: The launch of an agentic AI trip concierge by Travelxp relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on agentic capabilities for human-AI teaming.

slides.title: ReWeight: Leveraging Human Data for VLA Post-Training via Demonstration Retrieval and Sample Weighting
slides.highlight: This framework uses optimal transport to retrieve relevant egocentric human demonstrations and weight them to reduce cross-embodiment discrepancies, aligning with MOSAIC's use of ego-exo views and Optimal Transport for human-AI alignment.

card.one_liner: ReWeight improves VLA post-training by selectively retrieving and weighting human demonstrations based on cross-embodiment similarity.
card.key_idea: A framework using a cross-embodiment visuomotor encoder and optimal transport to retrieve relevant human data and assign sample-level weights based on behavioral discrepancy with robot data.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using π0.5 across 8 simulation and 4 real-world tasks. Success rates improved from 39% to 57% (simulation) and 40% to 68.8% (real-world).

slides.title: Learning Multimodal One-step Flow Policy via Value-weighted Optimal Transport
slides.tldr: OPTIMAL TRANSPORT FOR MULTIMODAL FLOW POLICIES
slides.highlight: This work introduces OptiFlow, which uses entropic optimal transport to learn one-step flow policies that capture multimodal behaviors without out-of-distribution divergence, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for intent alignment.

card.one_liner: OptiFlow learns efficient one-step flow policies for offline RL while preserving multimodal action distributions.
card.key_idea: It uses entropic optimal transport to couple one-step policy samples with a value-weighted reference flow policy, decoupling value guidance from geometric action-space alignment.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on OGBench (navigation, manipulation, visual) and D4RL (AntMaze, Adroit) benchmarks; results show superior performance and multimodal preservation over baselines like FQL.

slides.title: MedVA: An End-to-End Neuro-Symbolic Agentic System for Medical Volume Visualization
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC AGENT FOR MEDICAL VOLUME VISUALIZATION
slides.highlight: MedVA utilizes a neuro-symbolic agentic system to refine clinical intent and optimize ROI visualization, aligning with MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic and agent-based modeling.

card.one_liner: MedVA is a neuro-symbolic agentic system that automates clinically grounded medical volume visualization from natural language.
card.key_idea: It combines MLLMs with symbolic clinical knowledge for intent formulation, multi-model pretrained segmentation for ROI identification, and volume-based visibility objectives for visualization optimization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via agent-level quantitative analysis (Dice scores), system-level case studies on CT volumes, and a formative user study showing high usability.
